sources.title: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.section: Chapter 1 Chemical Reactions and Equations, section 1.2.1 Balanced Chemical Equations

nodes.statement: Balance a simple chemical equation by counting atoms of each element and changing only coefficients.
Hydrogen burns in oxygen to form water; the skeletal equation is H2 + O2 -> H2O.
In H2 + O2 -> H2O the left side has 2 hydrogen and 2 oxygen atoms; the right side has 2 hydrogen and 1 oxygen atom, so oxygen does not match.
Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction (law of conservation of mass), so each element must have the same number of atoms on both sides of the equation.
An equation is balanced by changing the coefficients written in front of formulas, never the subscripts inside a formula.
Changing a subscript changes the substance: H2O2 is hydrogen peroxide, a different compound from water, H2O.

steps: Oxygen: 2 on the left, 1 on the right. Put coefficient 2 in front of H2O: oxygen 2 and 2; hydrogen on the right becomes 4.
Hydrogen: 2 on the left, 4 on the right. Put coefficient 2 in front of H2: hydrogen 4 and 4.
Check every element: H 4 = 4, O 2 = 2. Balanced: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O.

nodes.statement: Fix the oxygen count by writing H2O2, that is, by changing a subscript.
nodes.why_wrong: Changing a subscript changes the substance (H2O2 is hydrogen peroxide); only coefficients may change.

nodes.statement: The equation is shown without physical states or reaction conditions.
nodes.what_is_lost: State symbols (g, l) and the conditions of burning hydrogen are not shown; the video counts atoms only.

nodes.stem: In H2 + O2 -> H2O, count the oxygen atoms on each side. Which side is short?
nodes.answer: The right side: 1 oxygen atom against 2 on the left.
